newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan Tamil refugees leave rebel-held north.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan Tamil refugees leave rebel-held north.

text.p: More Tamil refugees are leaving regions controlled by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels in Sri Lanka's north and are trickling into army-held areas, a military spokesman said on Tuesday.
"They are unhappy with the (rebels) and want to get away from the shortages of food and medicine in (rebel-held) areas," the spokesman said.
"Also, they hear from other civilians that conditions in army-held areas are returning to normal," he added. "Those who have come over have told the army that many others are waiting to come across."
More than 3,000 refugees had arrived by boat in the northern Jaffna peninsula from areas of the northern Wanni mainland under rebel control in the period from March 10 to Monday, the spokesman said.
Most of the returning refugees had been displaced from their homes in Jaffna because of fighting between government forces and the LTTE rebels.
The spokesman said many refugees were also arriving in north-central Vavuniya, the gateway to the Wanni mainland.
Almost 60,000 refugees had crossed over to Vavuniya since last October, of whom 43,775 have been sent to their homes in Jaffna and other parts of the north, he said.
Some 15,000 refugees were waiting at welfare centres in Vavuniya, about 225 km (140 miles) north of the capital Colombo, he added.
The military screens the refugees to prevent an infiltration of rebels, who are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the mainly Sinhalese island's north and east.
But the Tigers have accused the military of imposing restrictions on people travelling in and out of areas captured by the army.

The rebels said in a statement on Tuesday that the military had imposed numerous restrictions including exhaustive checks on civilians travelling between Vavuniya and northwestern Mannar, which was only recently linked to the rest of the island.
Mannar had remained cut off for almost a decade because of Tamil rebel activity.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year, but the rebels say the toll is higher.
